what_its_for: Tolvaptan is used to treat low sodium levels in your blood (a condition called hyponatremia) that can happen with heart failure, liver disease, or a kidney hormone disorder called SIADH. The brand Jynarque is specifically used to slow down the worsening of a kidney disease called autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). It works by helping your kidneys remove extra water from your body through your urine.
how_to_take: Take tolvaptan by mouth as a tablet, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it in the morning if possible. You must have access to water and be able to drink fluids freely while taking this medicine. Do NOT drink grapefruit juice while taking this medication. Do not crush or split the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition. For low sodium (Samsca), the usual starting dose is 15 mg once daily, which your doctor may increase to 30 mg or up to 60 mg per day. For polycystic kidney disease (Jynarque), the usual starting dose is 45 mg in the morning and 15 mg about 8 hours later, which may be increased over time. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. However, if it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next regular dose at the usual time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store tolvaptan tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your body and cause serious side effects. Avoid alcohol, as it may worsen side effects. Do not limit your water or fluid intake unless your doctor tells you to — you must be able to drink water freely. Avoid taking other medicines that can harm the liver without first talking to your doctor. Tell your doctor about all herbal supplements (especially St. John's Wort), vitamins, and other medications you take.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice), dark brown urine, unusual tiredness or weakness, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite (these could be signs of liver damage), extreme thirst or difficulty drinking fluids, signs of high sodium such as trouble speaking, confusion, or seizures, rapid or irregular heartbeat, fainting or dizziness, or difficulty urinating. Tell your doctor about any new or worsening symptoms. Because of the risk of serious liver problems, Jynarque is only available through a special program called a REMS program and requires regular liver blood tests.
when_it_works: You may notice increased urination within a few hours of taking your first dose — this is normal and means the medicine is working. Improvements in sodium levels or fluid balance are usually seen within the first few days. For polycystic kidney disease, the benefit is seen over months to years as it helps slow down kidney decline. Do not stop taking the medicine without talking to your doctor, even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tolvaptan may harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor immediately if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, especially dehydration and changes in sodium levels. Kidney disease: Jynarque should not be used if you cannot urinate. Liver disease: Samsca is not recommended for patients with liver problems. Both forms of tolvaptan require regular monitoring of your liver through blood tests. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been fully established. Always inform all of your healthcare providers that you are taking tolvaptan.
